thread:
alex: flagging a design question for bulk rotate + empty-state handling. we have a few edge-cases when customers rotate many keys at once. thoughts?
neha: nice. what's the primary risk we want to solve in the flow? accidental mass-revoke? broken integrations?
alex: both. product asks for a safe default so accidental wide-scale outages are rare. also want the empty state after rotate to surface next steps clearly.
jess: for bulk rotate UX: require a typed confirm when >5 keys selected? e.g., type "ROTATE" to continue. reduces fat-finger risk.
rob: ops pushback: typed confirm adds friction for automated workflows. maybe gate only in UI but allow API to proceed.
neha: agree — UI can be stricter. also show a preview table: old key name + owner + last-used timestamp so people can catch mistakes.
alex: good. accessibility check: keyboard users need to be able to shift-select ranges and tab through the preview. avoid modal traps where focus disappears.
aria-bot: accessibility reminder: when using dialog, set focus to the heading and trap focus inside. Provide an accessible name and use aria-modal. For typed confirmations also expose instructions with aria-describedby.
jess: copy debate: current CTA says "Rotate keys". some PMs prefer "Issue replacements". which is clearer to end-users?
neha: my vote for plain language: "Replace keys" or "Rotate keys" are both ok; "Issue replacements" sounds more technical. also microcopy should say what happens to the old keys.
rob: backend timeline: we can provision new tokens immediately but we can keep old tokens valid for a configurable grace period (default 0s, org-configurable up to 10m). we should surface the chosen grace window in the modal.
alex: proposal for modal body copy (compact):
```
Heading: "Rotate selected API keys"
Body: "Generating replacements will create new tokens and optionally keep the current tokens active for a short grace period so services can update. You will only be shown new tokens once."
Grace option label: "Grace period (minutes)"
Confirm typed label (if >5): "Type REPLACE to confirm"
Primary CTA: "Replace keys"
Cancel CTA: "Cancel"
```
jess: tiny nit: "You will only be shown new tokens once" is accurate but scary. maybe soften: "Make sure to copy your new tokens; they wont be shown again in the console."
neha: alternate: "Save each new token to your secure store. Tokens cannot be retrieved later from the console." clearer for security-minded folks.
rob: audit trail note: log who initiated the rotate, method (UI/API), selected keys, and grace period. send an org-level email when bulk rotates >50 keys.
aria-bot: privacy/audit notice: ensure logs redact tokens and avoid leaking key material in plaintext to logs. store only fingerprints where possible.
alex: empty state after rotate (when list becomes empty) — current empty state graphic shows "No credentials" with a single CTA "Create your first key". for bulk rotate we need a different path: success lined with next steps: show a short list of newly created token names and a CTA to copy/export them.
jess: design thought: after rotate success show a persistent download link (CSV) for 1 minute to let users export tokens. also show a clear warning: "This CSV contains secrets. Treat it securely."
neha: CSV download window is handy. make it keyboard accessible and announce via aria-live region: "Download available for 60 seconds".
rob: security: generated tokens must be printed once and then only available via the CSV for X seconds. implement short-lived S3 link with tokenized access.
alex: analytics: track `credential.rotate.bulk.started`, `credential.rotate.bulk.completed`, `credential.rotate.bulk.exported`. include prop `grace_minutes` and `confirm_type: [typed, none]`.
aria-bot: a11y quick checklist: focus order in bulk modal, typed confirm input label association, visible focus outlines for table rows, announce CSV availability via aria-live, ensure color contrast for banners is >=4.5:1.
jess: UI polish: for the empty-state copy after rotate, suggestion: "All selected credentials have been replaced. Download the new tokens now — you'll only see them once." with a small link to docs: "How to rotate without downtime".
neha: let's file follow-ups: design task (update mocks + CSV UX), dev task (export plumbing + analytics + audit), security task (S3 link TTL + redaction), copy task (final microcopy).
alex: i'll drop a new figma frame and tag people. quick hallway test w/ 4 engineers and 2 PMs next Tue. thanks! :white_check_mark:
